summary: HETA proposes a three-component attribution framework for decoder-only LLMs, combining target-conditioned attention rollout, Hessian-vector-product sensitivity, and KL-based masking impact, and reports large improvements on both established faithfulness metrics and a new curated dataset. The motivation (attention is not causal; first-order gradients miss curvature) is reasonable and the multi-signal integration is sensible, but the paper's contribution is largely a combination of existing ideas, the method is under-specified in key places, and the reported gains are so large (often 2–4× the next baseline) that fairness of the comparison is unclear without stronger controls, significance tests, and per-component evidence on more than one model. The claims of setting a 'new standard' are not adequately supported by the current evidence base.
strengths: Well-motivated critique of attention-only and first-order attribution for autoregressive models, with a concrete illustrative construction (Sec. 2) showing where gradients vanish but finite perturbations still matter.

The three-way integration of causal gating (attention rollout to target), curvature (HVP-based Hessian sensitivity), and information-theoretic masking (KL) is a coherent design that plausibly captures effects each component misses individually.

Evaluation goes beyond a single benchmark: Soft-NC/Soft-NS on three established datasets (LongRA, TellMeWhy, WikiBio), a curated NarrativeQA+SciQ mixed-paragraph probe, robustness to Gaussian perturbations, active/passive rephrasing, and a decoding-hyperparameter sweep.
Practical scalability considerations (low-rank rank-64 HVP, windowing, layer sampling for the 70B model) are explicitly addressed with a documented default configuration.
The DSA construction (predictive segment vs. distractor narrative) is a nice controlled probe of target-conditioned attribution precision that complements perturbation-based faithfulness.

key_concerns.issue: The magnitude of the reported improvements is inconsistent with typical attribution literature and is not adequately explained. On Soft-NC/Soft-NS (Table 3), HETA scores ~9–10 while every baseline sits at ~1–3; on DSA (Table 1), HETA is 4.25–5.10 while gradient/attention baselines are negative. Such gaps should be paired with per-instance paired significance tests, baseline-tuning details (baseline hyperparameters, prompt/format equivalence, whether baselines had access to the same attention layers/heads), and a sanity check that the metric implementation used across methods is identical.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add paired significance tests (bootstrap or Wilcoxon) for HETA vs. each baseline per dataset/model; document baseline hyperparameter tuning; release per-instance metric traces; and include a sanity control (e.g., HETA reduced to attention rollout only) plotted on the same axis to verify the metric scale.

key_concerns.issue: The final attribution score in equation 5 is typeset ambiguously (Attr = MT[i] β S + γ I versus MT[i](βS+γI)), and β=γ=0.5 is stated without justification or a sensitivity sweep. Because MT[i] is a simplex-normalized gate, its multiplication with an un-normalized S and I fundamentally determines behavior, and readers cannot reproduce the score without disambiguation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Give equation 5 unambiguously with parentheses, show a (β,γ) sensitivity heatmap on at least one dataset/model, and report the normalization scheme applied to S and I before combination.

key_concerns.issue: Ablations (Fig. 2, Sec. 5.5) are conducted only on GPT-J 6B on TellMeWhy/etc., yet the paper claims each component is necessary across four models. There is no per-model ablation showing e.g. that Hessian-only vs. transition-only tradeoffs are stable across Phi-3, LLaMA-70B, Qwen2.5.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Repeat the six-config ablation at least on Phi-3 and Qwen2.5, and report per-metric deltas with error bars.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is thin at the component level: attention rollout (Abnar & Zuidema), Hessian-vector-product sensitivity (Pearlmutter; Hutchinson) and KL-under-masking are all off-the-shelf. The paper does not clearly demonstrate that the combination provides a mathematically justified improvement beyond 'more signal is better.' The 'theoretical properties and error bounds' are deferred to an appendix that is not available in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State the specific new claim (e.g., an axiomatic property HETA satisfies that no baseline does), and either surface a key theorem from Appendix A2 into the main text or motivate the combination with an ablation-derived error decomposition.

key_concerns.issue: The curated dataset's ground-truth labels are the intersection of GPT-4o and 'GPT-5 Thinking' spans, and the F1-alignment metric also uses these LLM-derived annotations. This risks circularity — the target explanations were produced by frontier LLMs, and HETA is evaluated with respect to LLM-style rationales. Human validation is not described.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a human-annotation study on a stratified subsample (a few hundred instances) with inter-annotator agreement vs. the GPT annotators, and report DSA/F1 on the human subset.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is thin. Std '<0.2' or '<±0.06' is asserted without confidence intervals or effect sizes, no significance test is reported anywhere in Tables 1–3, and only three seeds are used.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report explicit ±std/CI in every cell of Tables 1–3, run more seeds where feasible, and add paired significance tests for the headline comparisons.

key_concerns.issue: Table 3 contains anomalous entries — e.g., LLaMA-3.1-70B Attention Rollout Soft-NC = −1.48 and Soft-NS = 0.01, then 1.48 later in the row; several other entries have signs that are hard to interpret. This casts doubt on either the metric implementation or the transcription.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Audit Table 3 for transcription errors; state the sign convention for Soft-NC/Soft-NS and their expected range; explain why attention rollout is negative on 70B but positive on Phi-3/GPT-J.

key_concerns.issue: Related-work discussion of ContextCite, TDD, Peering, ReAgent is critical but not always fair (e.g., ContextCite is described as 'sentence-level' only, while its formulation is per-source and can operate at finer granularity). Positioning would benefit from a small taxonomy table.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a related-methods comparison table (granularity, causal vs correlational, curvature-aware, hyperparameter-stable, cost) and soften unsupported characterizations.

key_concerns.issue: Writing has recurring readability issues: garbled equations for MT and DSA, run-on sentences, inconsistent notation between the algorithm (Πi, HT, S(T)_i) and the surrounding prose, and undefined symbols (e.g., 'x'i' in the robustness formula).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Copy-edit for grammar, re-typeset display equations, and add a notation table.

questions_for_authors: Please disambiguate equation 5: is the score MT[i]·(β·S + γ·I) or MT[i]·β·S + γ·I, and how are S and I scaled before combination?

How were baseline hyperparameters tuned per model/dataset? For gradient methods (IG, Input×Grad), what baseline, number of steps, and integration path were used, and are those tuning choices comparable across methods?

Under what implementation of Soft-NC/Soft-NS on generative LMs is a score of >9 achievable for one method while others cluster at 1–2? Please give the exact perturbation schedule (fraction masked, sampling of the target, etc.) and confirm it is identical across methods.
Do the improvements hold under a paired significance test (Wilcoxon signed-rank) per instance, and what is the effect size?
Please provide per-model ablations (not just GPT-J) for the six configurations in Sec. 5.5.

For the 70B model, second-order terms are computed only in the last six layers — was this choice tuned on evaluation data (risking leakage) or fixed a priori? A sensitivity plot over 'k last layers' would help.
The curated-dataset labels come from GPT-4o ∩ GPT-5 spans; does DSA/F1 hold up on a human-annotated subset?
What is the runtime/memory cost of HETA vs. ContextCite, ReAgent, and IG on the 70B model in practice, and how does the low-rank+windowing variant compare to the full estimator on quality?

The attention rollout used is 'target-conditioned' — please specify precisely (which path aggregation formula, treatment of residuals, softmax vs raw attention) since rollout has multiple non-equivalent definitions.
calibration_check: Claims of 'new state of the art' and 'new standard for interpretability' are not scoped to the evidence provided: gains are large but rest on one lightly-audited metric set, one non-ablated dataset for ablations, LLM-derived labels, and no significance testing.

significance.justification: Attribution for decoder-only LLMs is a live problem the ICLR community cares about, but the paper's incremental combination and lack of downstream evidence (e.g., debugging, hallucination localization) limit real-world impact.

novelty.justification: Each component (attention rollout, HVP-based curvature, KL-under-masking) is off-the-shelf; the contribution is the integration and a curated dataset, which is useful but not a fundamentally new mechanism.

rigor.justification: Suspiciously large baseline gaps, ambiguous equation 5, ablations on only one model, and reliance on LLM-derived ground truth together undermine confidence that the claim–evidence link is tight.

statistical_soundness.justification: Only three seeds, informal std bounds ('<0.2', '±0.06'), no significance tests, no confidence intervals, and no per-instance paired comparisons for headline claims.

calibration_honesty.justification: Sweeping claims of a 'new standard' and 'consistently outperforms' with margins that are not statistically stress-tested; limitations mentioned only for runtime, not evaluation.

clarity.justification: Structure is standard but the method's key equation is ambiguous, notation is inconsistent, and the DSA formula in prose is garbled — a reader cannot reimplement HETA from the text alone.

structure_compliance.justification: Follows the conventional Introduction/Motivation/Background/Method/Experiments/Ablation/Related Work/Conclusion structure at typical ICLR length.

reproducibility.justification: Hardware, sequence lengths, β=γ=0.5, rank-64, six-layer sampling on 70B are stated, but attention rollout variant, S/I normalization, baseline tuning, exact Soft-NC/NS implementation, and dataset construction (beyond a snippet) are under-specified.

related_work.justification: Key baselines (ContextCite, TDD, Peering, ReAgent) are named and critiqued, but characterizations occasionally overstate limitations of prior work, and there is no compact positioning table.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative content (ablation bars, sensitivity/robustness/F1, qualitative distributions), though Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 conflate too many panels and Table 3 appears to contain transcription anomalies.

breadth_generality.justification: Four models across scales are tested for headline metrics, but ablations, robustness stress tests, and human validation are all confined to a single model/dataset, weakening the paper's generality claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: the framework is sensible and the empirical envelope is broad, but rigor, calibration, and specification issues make the current version fall below the ICLR bar without a substantive revision.
